name: Santiago Xanica Zapotec
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible
sweep_summary: Santiago Xanica Zapotec is not in the catalog. The single sweep item (Penner et al. 2008, LSVT prosody in Parkinson's patients, German-language clinical journal) is a Glottolog mis-assignment - its record says 'computerized assignment from \"lee\"' (Lee Silverman) - and has nothing to do with Zapotec; the 5.3 live table lists only Piper 1995 and Broadwell 2015 for sant1452. No first-hand word-stress statement for this variety was found anywhere. The closest thing read is Piper 1995 (SIL Mexico Workpapers 11, fetched sources via Wayback, scanned), p. 68 fn. 9: Xanica Zapotec has contrastive tone not written in the orthography and plain/laryngealized/glottalized/aspirated nuclei - silent on stress. The SIL archive holds 15 zpr items (2015 snapshot); the two that could carry a pronunciation note - 'Breve vocabulario' (1993) and 'Frases ilustrativas' (1993) - are Cloudflare-blocked downloads with no Wayback copy; the cultural-texts scan is handwritten; the primers say nothing. The one phonological description, Piper 1990 'Del protozapoteco al zapoteco de Xanica: un estudio fonológico' (22 pp., unpublished), has no located copy and is the high-priority acquisition. they are flagged in and were not used). searching went through Crossref, archive.org, Wayback, Glottolog and SIL directly.

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Piper 1995 (narrative discourse functions of 'lee') and Broadwell 2015 (comparative aspect) listed; no phonological description of Santiago Xanica Zapotec found.

new_statements.quote: The phonemes of XZ are listed here with orthographical symbols, where different, given in parentheses: p, t, c (ts), ky (ky), k, kw (kw), b (b), d, f (only loanwords), s, š (x), z, ž (zh), m, n, ñ, ngw (ngw), l, r, w, y, i, e, ə (ë), u, o, a. The syllable nucleus may be a simple vowel: a; laryngealized: a' (aa); glottalized: aʔ (a'); or aspirated: ah (ah). There is contrastive tone in XZ, which is not represented in the practical orthography.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule available: the only accessible first-hand phonological remark says Xanica Zapotec has contrastive tone (unwritten in the practical orthography) and says nothing about stress or accent placement. (scanned rendering of IPA symbols in the quote is approximate: ts, ky, kw, b, x, zh, ngw, ë are the orthographic equivalents shown in parentheses.)
new_statements.domain_note: Footnote-level phonological sketch in a discourse paper; concerns the phoneme inventory and syllable nucleus, not the word or phrase. No stress statement anywhere in the 12 pages.
new_statements.identity_note: Sources are all by Michael J. and Priscila Piper (SIL) on the Santiago Xanica town variety ('XZ'). Glottolog sant1452 = ISO zpr, classified Central Core Zapotec > Cisyautepequeño (sout3003) after Beam de Azcona 2004 / Campbell 2017. Ethnologue-derived alternative names on the Glottolog page include 'Zapoteco de Asunción Tlacolulita' (a different Yautepec-district town) and Campbell et al. 2022 label 8794-zpr 'Coatlán Zapotec'; treat those as name confusions, not attestations of the same variety.

Xánica stub has no phonology; the family article only says varieties described as having stress (e.g. Isthmus) put it on the penultimate syllable of the root, prefixes and clitics not affecting it - not a statement about Xanica.
